works.title: A Body of Practical Divinity
works.author: Thomas Watson
works.edition: Glasgow: Blackie & Son, 1859. A Body of Practical Divinity, in a series of sermons on the Shorter Catechism of the Westminster Assembly, to which are appended select sermons on various subjects, together with The Art of Divine Contentment and Christ's Various Fulness

files.contents: The whole work in one volume. It has the preface 'To the Reader' and a short account of the author, then the sermons on the Shorter Catechism, including the Ten Commandments and the Lord's Prayer (to p. 544, 'End of the author's lectures on the catechism'). Then come seven select sermons (Sermon VI, on Col. 3:11 'Christ is all in all', is Christ's Various Fulness), The Art of Divine Contentment (pp. 609-654), The Preciousness of the Soul, The Soul's Malady and Cure, The Beauty of Grace, and The Trees of Righteousness Blossoming (to p. 688), and finally Blackie's advertisements.

works.title: The Ten Commandments
works.author: Thomas Watson
works.edition: In A Body of Practical Divinity. Glasgow: Blackie & Son, 1859.
works.notes: The Ten Commandments was never printed on its own before 1931; none is on archive.org. It is part of A Body of Practical Divinity (entry watson-a-body-of-practical-divinity). The auto pick was an unrelated Seneca translation. The 1807 volume 1 already accepted for that entry (bodyofpractical01wats) holds this section too, but it is printed with the long s. I recommend switching the Body entry to this complete 1859 Glasgow one-volume edition; see the watson-the-lord-s-prayer notes.

works.title: The Lord's Prayer
works.author: Thomas Watson
works.edition: In A Body of Practical Divinity. Glasgow: Blackie & Son, 1859.
works.notes: The Lord's Prayer was never printed on its own before 1931. The 1890 Passmore & Alabaster split, and Banner of Truth's titles, are not on archive.org. It is the last part of A Body of Practical Divinity (entry watson-a-body-of-practical-divinity). The auto pick was an unrelated J. S. Watson book. Problem with that entry: accepted.json gives it bodyofpractical01wats, which is only volume 1 of the 1807 two-volume London (Baynes) printing, and it uses the long s ('fpeak', 'Chrift'). The Lord's Prayer is in that printing's volume 2 (bodyofpractical02wats), which was not taken. I recommend switching watson-a-body-of-practical-divinity to bodyofpracticald00watsuoft. It is the complete Glasgow 1859 one-volume edition in modern type, and I checked that it holds the Ten Commandments and all the Lord's Prayer petitions. It also includes The Art of Divine Contentment.
